title: True Truth
author: Chris Hobbs
summary: Chris Hobbs argues that Christian school leaders should view every subject, programme, technology and cultural shift through the lens of Scripture rather than reading Scripture through the lens of their own experience. He begins with a personal image of his wife's new reading glasses and a mentor's illustration of holding a child's photo and a Bible in opposite positions. Citing Francis Schaeffer's idea of true truth and C.S. Lewis on seeing everything by the light of Christianity, he says communities end up with bizarre school content when they do not start from foundational biblical truth. He lists what leaders gain from this lens: wisdom about organising a student-forming school, the anchor point of each discipline, discernment between light and heat in cultural conflict, and the ability to tell enduring goodness from fads. He closes that popular leadership frameworks are useful, but the Bible should come first.
points: Leaders should look at their school and its experiences through the lens of Scripture rather than reading Scripture through the lens of current experience.
When parents ask how a bizarre teaching reached their child's school, the root cause is usually a failure to begin from foundational truth, so starting points shape where the ball lands.
Scripture offers leaders models for organising a school, handling parent conflict and understanding human nature, as well as an anchor point for each academic discipline.
Christ's habit of asking questions models both good pedagogy and a calm way to present truth as light rather than heat.
Secular leadership frameworks such as Lencioni, Collins and EOS remain useful, but the author insists they should be applied after the biblical lens, not before.
quotes: Don’t look at Scripture through the lens of your experience. Look at your experience through the lens of Scripture.
God’s Word is the lens through which we view every subject, pedagogical enhancement, technological innovation, programmatic addition, and cultural shift.
The Bible is not an exhaustive textbook for every academic discipline. It does, however, provide a clear lens through which we can study them all.
Parents often erupt in righteous indignation: “How’d we get here?” when they uncover a bizarre teaching at their child’s school. The answer is simple. You didn’t start with the true truth.
Every academic domain has its anchor point in Scripture. Do the work to know the core truth of your discipline as Scripture states it.
Jesus’ model of question-asking is great pedagogy. It is also a powerful testimony to the sufficiency of true truth.
But before you reach for any of them, make sure you are viewing your institution through the perfectly clarifying lens of the Bible. It’s amazing what you’ll see.
